poster_title: Generalist Reward Models: Found Inside Large Language Models
authors: Yi-Chen Li, Tian Xu, Yang Yu, Xuqin Zhang, Xiong-Hui Chen, Zhongxiang Ling, Ningjing Chao, Lei Yuan, Zhi-Hua Zhou

panels.headline: Costly human-labeled data for reward models
content: Alignment of LLMs with human values is a central challenge.
Current methods like RLHF require expensive human preference datasets.
Alternative methods like RLAIF lack theoretical foundation and can inherit biases.

panels.headline: High-quality, expensive human-labeled data
content: Need for high-quality, expensive human-labeled data to train reward models.
Lack of principled method to extract reward signals from LLMs without further training.

panels.headline: Logits as soft Q-function
content: Discovery of a generalist reward model within any LLM trained via standard next-token prediction.
Theoretical proof that the reward function from offline IRL can be recovered from the next-token prediction objective.
Proof that fine-tuning a model with its own endogenous reward leads to a policy with a provably superior error bound.

panels.headline: RM-Bench and Multifacted-Bench
content: Extensive experiments validating the theoretical findings.
Comparison with existing LLM-as-a-judge methods and explicitly trained reward models.
panels.figure_caption: Response classification accuracy by reward models on the RM-Bench

panels.headline: Outperforms existing LLM-as-a-judge approaches
content: The method outperforms existing LLM-as-a-judge approaches.
The method can surpass the performance of reward models trained on expensive human-labeled data.
panels.figure_caption: Response classification accuracy on the Multifacted-Bench

panels.headline: More efficient and theoretically grounded paradigm
content: The reward modeling stage can be replaced by eliciting the knowledge already captured during pre-training.
This approach heralds a more efficient, powerful, and theoretically grounded paradigm for LLM alignment and multi-modal models.
